input.body:
Closes #1652

Owner decision: *"assume that all repos are behaving correctly and clean up after themselves in 1
week, and do the cleanup then … the canon will never know the state of all active or inert repos
that use it."*

#1645 landed the opposite — a removal gated on a condition that *reads back true*, and where that
condition was unreadable, building the census was to be the chain's first link. That is the
failure the rule exists to prevent. A project cannot enumerate the things consuming it, so "no
holder still carries the old shape" never reads true, the removal never falls due, and the
tolerance is permanent while looking scheduled. #1639 was the mistake made concrete: a fleet
census as the precondition for every cleanup.

## What replaces it

The window: how long a correctly-behaving holder needs to pick the advisory up and act on it,
written as the date the removal link waits on. A holder that ignored the advisory for that long
takes the break.

A count is still the right gate **where you own both sides of it and it actually comes back** —
"the oldest row in the retention window postdates the rename" — and the skill now says exactly
that and stops there, rather than presenting the census as the rigorous default.

## The purge

The old decision was stated in nine places besides the rule itself; a reversal that only edits the
sentence the owner replied to leaves the rest teaching the world that was just retired.

| Where | Was |
|---|---|
| `packs/basics/RULES.md` + `writing-migration-plans` | "a condition that reads back true … never a date", and the unreadable-gate-is-the-first-link paragraph |
| the same skill's phase checklist | an exit-condition example — "every member's stamp shows the new ref" — that assumed another repo's state is observable from here |
| the local pack's standing decision (12) | "gate it on a converge-cycle-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date alone" — this one said it first |
| `renamed-packs.mjs` | "RETIREMENT is read off the fleet, never off a calendar" |
| `settings-file-names.mjs`, `repo-context.mjs`, `version.mjs`, the settings-file-rename record | the same gate at four tolerance sites |
| `task-contract.mjs`, `queue/secrets-bag.mjs` | "while members still declare them", "gated on no member still stamping a bag" |
| `legacy-shape-in-use`, `legacy-task-fields` | both `why` strings told a repo it was holding a gate shut |

Both references docs carry the reversal with the owner's own words, so the next review pass sees
why the earlier phrasing was replaced rather than re-deriving it.

## The chain

#1639 is closed (not planned) and #1638's four removal links are re-gated: `Blocked-by: #1637`,
`Not-before: 2026-09-10` — a week after the advisories shipped. `Automerge: nothing` stays on
#1640 and #1641, unchanged: a repo that missed the window gets no pack rather than a degraded one,
and that is still past what a later PR undoes.

`node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 3157 pass, 0 fail. `check_the_world` 0 blocking,
`ci-work-scope` clean. No behaviour changes here: the diff is prose, comments and the four pack
version rows, so what the tests prove is that nothing else moved.

content.content:
Almost every migration ships one: a dual read, an accepted old spelling, a decode map, a shim at
the path something was renamed from. It is what lets the two halves of the migration land in
either order, and it is the single most reliable way for a migration to never finish — because
once it works, nothing in the world complains about it. A tolerance is not part of the end state.
It is the ladder, and the plan says when the ladder comes down.

Three things ship *with* it, in the same stack, never afterwards:

- **The advisory.** Whoever still holds the old shape must be told, at the point they hold it —
  the check that reads their file, the warning the loader emits, the finding their own run
  reports. A tolerance with no advisory asks people to migrate off something they have no way of
  knowing they are on, and then measures how few of them did. Where the tolerance is in code the
  holders cannot see, the advisory is the one that fires in *their* repo, not a note in yours.
- **The removal, written now.** It is code, so it goes in the approved stack with everything else
  (above); what waits is its merge, and the thing that performs that merge is a link in the chain.
- **The window that releases it** — how long a correctly-behaving holder needs to pick the
  advisory up and act on it, written as the date the removal link waits on. The tempting
  alternative is a census — "when no holder still carries the old shape" — and it is usually
  unanswerable: a project cannot see which of the things consuming it are live, which are
  dormant and which stopped updating months ago, so the removal waits on an answer that never
  arrives and the tolerance becomes permanent while looking scheduled. Read a count only where
  you own both sides of it and it really does come back ("the oldest row in the retention window
  postdates the rename"). Everywhere else, pick the window, say in the link what it assumes, and
  let a holder that ignored the advisory for that long take the break.

Say at the tolerance site which link removes it, so the next reader of that code is looking at a
scheduled removal rather than a permanent-looking feature with an optimistic comment beside it.

Closes #1652

Owner decision: **"the canon will never know the state of all active or inert repos that use it."**
The week that came with it — *"assume that all repos are behaving correctly and clean up after
themselves in 1 week, and do the cleanup then"* — sized #1638's cleanup; it is that change's
window, not a constant, and later ones may ride major version releases instead.

#1645 landed the opposite — a removal gated on a condition that *reads back true*, and where that
condition was unreadable, building the census was to be the chain's first link. That is the
failure the rule exists to prevent. A project cannot enumerate the things consuming it, so "no
holder still carries the old shape" never reads true, the removal never falls due, and the
tolerance is permanent while looking scheduled. #1639 was the mistake made concrete: a fleet
census as the precondition for every cleanup.

## What replaces it

The window: how long a correctly-behaving holder needs to pick the advisory up and act on it,
written as the date the removal link waits on, and **sized by the change that ships it**. A holder
that ignored the advisory for that long takes the break.

A count is still the right gate **where you own both sides of it and it actually comes back** —
"the oldest row in the retention window postdates the rename" — and the skill now says exactly
that and stops there, rather than presenting the census as the rigorous default.

## The purge

The old decision was stated in nine places besides the rule itself; a reversal that only edits the
sentence the owner replied to leaves the rest teaching the world that was just retired.

| Where | Was |
|---|---|
| `packs/basics/RULES.md` + `writing-migration-plans` | "a condition that reads back true … never a date", and the unreadable-gate-is-the-first-link paragraph |
| the same skill's phase checklist | an exit-condition example — "every member's stamp shows the new ref" — that assumed another repo's state is observable from here |
| the local pack's standing decision (12) | "gate it on a converge-cycle-confirmable precondition, never a calendar date alone" — this one said it first |
| `renamed-packs.mjs` | "RETIREMENT is read off the fleet, never off a calendar" |
| `settings-file-names.mjs`, `repo-context.mjs`, `version.mjs`, the settings-file-rename record | the same gate at four tolerance sites |
| `task-contract.mjs`, `queue/secrets-bag.mjs` | "while members still declare them", "gated on no member still stamping a bag" |
| `legacy-shape-in-use`, `legacy-task-fields` | both `why` strings told a repo it was holding a gate shut |

Both references docs carry the reversal with the owner's own words — the durable half separated
from the week, so a later reader does not read #1638's window as policy.

The tolerance sites that name a week (`renamed-packs.mjs`, `version.mjs`, the settings-file-rename
record, both advisory rules) keep it: that is #1638's actual window, stated where the removal is
scheduled, which is where a specific date belongs.

## The chain

#1639 is closed (not planned) and #1638's four removal links are re-gated: `Blocked-by: #1637`,
`Not-before: 2026-09-10` — a week after the advisories shipped. `Automerge: nothing` stays on
#1640 and #1641, unchanged: a repo that missed the window gets no pack rather than a degraded one,
and that is still past what a later PR undoes.

`ci-work-scope` clean. No behaviour changes here: the diff is prose, comments and the four pack
version rows, so what the tests prove is that nothing else moved.

own comments gated themselves on a census — renamed-packs, settings-file-names,
